name: Cuartel del Conde-Duque

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/73436 (centroid of the outline; long sides at 26.7°, the main front on calle del Conde Duque faces 116.7°)

rights.note: Barracks of the Royal Guardias de Corps, begun in 1717 to Pedro de Ribera's design (portal and works until c. 1730). Upper floors burnt in 1869; restored as a cultural centre by Julio Cano Lasso (from 1969) and Carlos de Riaño (2009–2011). The design is in the public domain; the model follows the restored building.

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q5191859_cuartel_del_conde_duque.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. The whole block on the OSM plan: red brick on a granite plinth, rusticated granite quoins at the outer corners, four rows of openings (windows, oculi) with granite frames, moulded cornice at 17 m; on the west the street lies 3–11 m lower and the granite basement with small windows shows. Ribera's portal on calle del Conde Duque is stylised (stacked carved piers, door 4.4 × 7 m, cartouche with garlands, broken pediment, the royal arms with crown and cross at 15.8 m). Main courtyard: the white central body of the rear range (giant pilasters, attic with the arms, curved shoulders, urns and four pinnacles to ~32.5 m) and the stone podium with its steps; courtyard walls brick below, cream render on the top floor. Grey zinc roofs, red tiles on the rear range (as on the orthophoto), hipped at the outer corners, 30°/24° pitches estimated. Courtyard floors level at y = 0, coloured from the PNOA orthophoto (it shows the temporary stage and tents of the summer events in the main courtyard). Uncertain: heights (±10 %), exact window count and rhythm (regular 4.5 m bays), the portal's carving, the roof pitches.
